## Keywords

{{< glossary digital-skills digital-literacy digital-competence digcomp competence-area proficiency-level labour-market lifelong-learning >}}

## 1.1 Skills, literacy, competence

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Digital skills** are practical abilities, like sharing a folder.
- **Digital literacy** adds understanding: find and check information safely.
- **Digital competence** adds attitudes: use the tools with responsibility.
- **Lab task:** Write five things you did on a computer this week. Which level is each one?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/skills-circles.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Which term, which level?

The levels are basic, intermediate and advanced.

a) A student makes a chart of test results in a spreadsheet. Which level is this?
b) Which level is programming a game server?
c) A student types fast but shares the password with friends. Do they have digital skills or digital competence?

::: {.answer}
a) intermediate
b) advanced
c) skills, but not competence
:::

## 1.2 DigComp 2.2: five areas

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- DigComp 2.2 is the European framework of digital competence.
- It has five areas: information, communication, content creation, safety and problem solving.
- Programming is only one of its 21 competences.
- **Lab task:** Do the DigComp self-check. Which is your strongest area?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/digcomp-areas.png)
:::
::::

## Eight proficiency levels

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Levels 1–2 (foundation): you work with help.
- Levels 3–4 (intermediate): you work alone.
- Levels 5–6 (advanced): you help others.
- Levels 7–8 (highly specialised): you lead and create new ways.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/proficiency.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Tasks in DigComp

A game studio lists four tasks.
**In which DigComp area is each task?**

::: {.reveal}
1. Is this forum post reliable? This is **information and data**.
2. Writing polite messages in the team chat is **communication**.
3. Checking the licence of a free sound is **content creation**.
4. "I cannot make a chart yet, so I take a course" is **problem solving**.
:::

## Try it 2 · Place it in DigComp

a) You set a screen lock on your phone. Which DigComp area is this?
b) In which area is writing polite messages in the team chat?
c) A person helps others to use a tool. Which level group is this?

::: {.answer}
a) safety
b) communication and collaboration
c) advanced
:::

## 1.3 The labour market

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Almost every job is digital now.
- Software does routine tasks, so people must use and check the tools.
- Tools change, so employers want **lifelong learning**.
- **Lab task:** Find a real job advert in games. Which DigComp areas do its requirements need?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/studio.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · Skills at work

a) What is the EU target for adults with basic digital skills by 2030?
b) What do we call learning new tools during the whole working life?
c) A job advert asks to "handle player data responsibly". Which DigComp area is this?

::: {.answer}
a) 80 %
b) lifelong learning
c) safety
:::

## Try it 4 · Read the candidates (harder)

The facts: the tester writes bug reports in a shared tracker. The marketing assistant makes short videos for social media.

a) In which DigComp area are bug reports in a shared tracker?
b) In which area are short videos for social media?
c) A candidate trains colleagues in a new tool. Which level group is this?

::: {.answer}
a) communication and collaboration
b) digital content creation
c) advanced
:::

## Summary

- Skills, literacy and competence: each one includes the one before.
- DigComp 2.2 has five areas and eight levels in four groups.
- Programming is only one of the 21 competences.
- Software does routine work, so every job needs digital skills.
- Lifelong learning starts with finding your own gaps.
